info.title: Flock Energy - Urja Meter Ops API
info.description:
A clean, documented REST API over the legacy **Urja Meter Ops** portal.

The portal has no API. This service logs in as a normal user, manages the session,
reverse-engineers the portal's internal endpoints, normalises its inconsistent payloads,
and exposes the result as typed JSON that another program can consume without ever
touching the portal.

**What it adds over the portal**

* Filtering, sorting and pagination the portal cannot do (make, status, phase, build,
  any hierarchy code).
* The network hierarchy, reconstructed from per-meter paths into a queryable tree.
* Real consumption, derived by differencing the portal's cumulative registers.
* Proximity search over meter coordinates.
* An explicit data-quality report instead of silently tidied-away inconsistencies.

See `PROTOCOL.md` for how the portal actually works, and `README.md` for design decisions
and trade-offs.

get.description:
Filter, sort and page the full meter estate.

Served from the local snapshot, so this supports filters the portal itself cannot: by make, status, phase, install type, build and any hierarchy code. All filters are ANDed. `search` matches meter id or serial as a literal substring - unlike the portal, `%` and `_` are not wildcards here.

get.description:
Energy **consumed**, derived by differencing the portal's cumulative registers.

The portal returns raw register totals; summing that column would overstate usage by orders of magnitude. Each interval here is the difference between consecutive readings. Sampling cadence is inferred from the data (30-minute for most meters, daily for some), never assumed.

The upstream series is a fixed ~7-day window and ignores date parameters, so `from`/`to` are applied locally.

get.description:
The utility's network tree (Zone -> Circle -> Division -> Subdivision -> Substation -> Feeder -> DT), reconstructed by folding together every meter's root-to-leaf path. The portal only ever exposes one meter's path at a time.

**Node identity is the full ancestor path, not the bare code.** Mid-level codes are not globally unique upstream - `D-01` occurs under three different circles - so `Z-01/C-01/D-01` and `Z-01/C-03/D-01` are distinct nodes. Collapsing them by code would silently merge unrelated parts of the network. See PROTOCOL.md.

`meter_count` is cumulative: it counts meters anywhere beneath the node.

get.description:
The DT registry, enriched with a live meter count from the snapshot.

This registry is treated as the **authoritative** source for DT names: some meter records carry a stale alias (`DT-007` appears as both 'Sanganer DT 7' and 'Old Malviya Nagar Xfmr'), and the registry value wins. The conflict is still reported at `/data-quality` rather than hidden.

get.description:
Is the process up? Never touches the portal.

Kept independent of upstream deliberately: if this depended on the portal, a portal outage would make an orchestrator kill and restart healthy pods, turning a degradation into an outage.

get.description:
Can this instance serve real traffic? Verifies the portal session is genuinely accepted upstream and that a snapshot exists.

Returns 503 when not ready, so a load balancer drains this instance instead of serving errors. A *stale* snapshot still counts as ready - degraded is better than down.

post.description:
Rebuild the index immediately, ignoring the TTL.

Deliberately unauthenticated in this build because the service has no auth model at all (see README, *What I intentionally left out*). It is idempotent and read-only with respect to the portal, but it does cost one upstream export, so it should sit behind auth and a rate limit before any real deployment.

Every inconsistency detected in the upstream data, aggregated with counts and sample meter ids.

This exists because hiding upstream mess behind a tidy API is how downstream teams end up debugging the wrong system. It also doubles as drift detection: if the portal's data changes, these counts move.

kwh.title: Kwh
kwh.description: Consumption in the interval (delta of register).

estimated.title: Estimated
estimated.description: True when the interval spans a gap in the upstream series.

ConsumptionInterval.title: ConsumptionInterval
ConsumptionInterval.description: Energy actually consumed between two consecutive readings.

readings.title: Readings
readings.description: Raw cumulative register readings. Included only when requested.

average_power_factor.title: Average Power Factor
average_power_factor.description: total_kwh / total_kvah. Null when kVAh is unavailable or zero.

peak_interval_kwh.title: Peak Interval Kwh
peak_interval_kwh.description: Largest single interval, at the granularity returned.

interval_minutes.title: Interval Minutes
interval_minutes.description: Modal sampling cadence inferred from the data, not assumed.

gap_count.title: Gap Count
gap_count.description: Missing sampling slots detected in the window.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable machine-readable slug. Branch on this, not on prose.

message.title: Message
message.description: Human-readable, safe to display. Never a stack trace.

details.title: Details
details.description: Optional structured context, e.g. invalid fields or a hint.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Correlation id; matches the X-Request-ID response header.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description: The body of an :class:`ApiError` as clients receive it.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description:
Envelope returned for **every** non-2xx response.

Declared so the OpenAPI document describes the real contract. Without it FastAPI
advertises its own ``HTTPValidationError`` for 422 and nothing at all for 404/5xx,
which makes generated clients fail to deserialise every error they receive.

data_quality.title: Data Quality

Meter.title: Meter
Meter.description: A smart meter, normalised across both upstream builds.

MeterBuild.title: MeterBuild
MeterBuild.description:
Which generation of the portal's data model a meter belongs to.

Not cosmetic: it determines the shape of the per-meter detail payload upstream
(``legacy`` -> parameter rows, ``v2`` -> a double-encoded ``classData`` blob).
Exposed because it explains data-quality differences a consumer will otherwise
find inexplicable.

MeterReading.title: MeterReading
MeterReading.description: One raw interval reading. ``kwh``/``kvah`` are **cumulative register values**.

MeterSummary.title: MeterSummary
MeterSummary.description: List-view projection. Omits the full hierarchy path to keep pages small.

distance_km.title: Distance Km
distance_km.description: Great-circle distance from the query point.

source.title: Source
source.description: Which upstream path produced it: 'export' or 'search'.

SnapshotInfo.title: SnapshotInfo
SnapshotInfo.description: Provenance for the local index - lets a caller reason about staleness itself.

meter_count.description: Meters attached, per the current snapshot.
